title: Book Two · Chapter 159: A Question at the Counter
story:
Mr Qiu has three small signs on his counter. One gives prices. One shows the opening times. The third says that some books belong to him and are not for sale.

A woman lifts a blue book from the end of the table.

“How much is this one?” she asks.

Mr Qiu is helping another customer choose paper. Ronan stands near the door with a new pencil in his hand.

“I think that one is his,” he says.

“Then why is it on the table?”

Ronan looks at the signs. The sign for Mr Qiu's own books is behind a tall packet of paper. The woman cannot see it from her side.

“Please wait a moment,” Ronan says. He turns to Mr Qiu. “Is the blue book for sale?”

“No. That is mine. The books on the other side are for sale.”

The woman puts it down. Mr Qiu offers her a thin storybook from the right-hand pile. She looks through it while he finishes with the paper customer.

Ronan points to the hidden sign.

“May I move that forward?”

“Yes. Keep the price sign clear too.”

Ronan tries the near corner. He goes outside to look. A box still hides the words. He moves the sign to the top of the low pile and steps back.

“Better?” Mr Qiu asks.

“I can read it from here.”

The woman can read it too. She thanks them, buys the thin book, and leaves with it in her bag.

Mr Qiu gives Ronan his pencil and change.

“You need a place on the floor next?” he asks.

“For what?”

“For all your steps back.”

Ronan looks down. He is almost in the street. He moves inside, and Mr Qiu laughs.

“The sign needs someone to read it,” Ronan says. “I was doing that job.”

“Bring the eyes closer to the doorway.”

Ronan sits on the low stool for a few minutes. Mr Qiu opens his own blue book. It is an ordinary afternoon. No one gives Ronan a practice mark for the sign.

At school the next day, he tells Mei about it. She asks if the sign can fall off the pile.

“I did not check that.”

“Paper can move.”

After lessons, Ronan goes back. The sign is still there, but Mr Qiu has put a small weight beside its base.

“I found a windy customer,” Mr Qiu says.

Ronan presses the base gently. It stays in place. He leaves it alone and buys no second pencil. At home, he sharpens the first pencil over a scrap of paper. He will use it for the next practice.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

for sale＝出售的；sign＝标牌；change＝找零；base＝底部。

## 理解问题

1. 顾客为什么误以为Mr Qiu自己的书也在出售？
2. Mei提醒了Ronan什么，Mr Qiu怎样处理？

## 读句子

**The woman puts it down.**

拆开看：The woman / puts / it down.

那个女人／把它／放下。
